s1.syndrome_frame: Painful swelling and ulceration of the glans penis with systemic symptoms
salient_findings: Painful swelling and ulceration of the glans penis
Grossly edematous glans penis and corona
Tender, firm ulcer on the ventral surface of the penis with overlying black eschar and granulation tissue
Dermal infiltrate of atypical lymphocytes on biopsy
Clonal IgH gene rearrangement on PCR analysis
FDG-avid abdominal and peripancreatic lymph nodes on PET-CT scan
key_facts: 78-year-old man presented with painful swelling and ulceration of the glans penis
Symptoms duration of 1 month
Previous medical history of elevated white blood cell count and inguinal lymphadenopathy
Previous treatments with topical antibiotics, antifungal agents, hydrogen peroxide soaks, warm compresses, and cephalexin showed no improvement
Routine blood test results were within normal limits
Cultures, assays, and blood tests evaluating for viral, bacterial, or fungal etiology were negative
Biopsy of the glans penis ulcer showed dermal infiltrate of atypical lymphocytes
Atypical lymphocytes were CD20+, CD79a+, and CD5+
PCR analysis revealed a clonal IgH gene rearrangement
PET-CT scan demonstrated FDG-avid abdominal and peripancreatic lymph nodes
Patient experienced fatigue, weight loss, and loss of appetite 4 years after initial presentation

s4.champion: Primary cutaneous diffuse large B-cell lymphoma

raw.champion: Primary cutaneous diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
raw.rationale: The presence of a dermal infiltrate of atypical lymphocytes that are CD20+, CD79a+, and CD5+ along with a clonal IgH gene rearrangement, and the fact that the patient's symptoms are localized to the skin, supports this diagnosis. The lack of response to topical treatments and the presence of systemic symptoms such as fatigue, weight loss, and loss of appetite also align with this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: While this is a possible diagnosis, the fact that the symptoms are localized to the skin and the presence of a clonal IgH gene rearrangement suggests a primary cutaneous origin.

rejected.label: Mantle cell lymphoma
rejected.why: This type of lymphoma typically presents with systemic symptoms and involvement of the lymph nodes, spleen, and bone marrow, which is not the primary presentation in this case.

rejected.label: Primary cutaneous marginal zone lymphoma
rejected.why: This type of lymphoma typically presents with smaller, more indolent lesions, and the immunophenotype does not match the one described in the case.

rejected.label: Follicular lymphoma
rejected.why: This type of lymphoma typically presents with systemic symptoms and involvement of the lymph nodes, spleen, and bone marrow, and the immunophenotype does not match the one described in the case.
